entry_state: The reserving exchange preserves each fitted mean, payment, status and joint draw. Failed and pending computation cannot be recoded as zero or probability mass. Resume requires a bound checkpoint and random state; documentary examples establish no runtime durability or calibrated forecast.
exit_state: Acquisition recoverability distinguishes whole-group and renewal inflows without counting a loss twice. Recognition consumes the remaining acquisition asset into the group and its CSM before premium receipt; balanced statements can still conceal duplicated assets and overstated margins.
findings: The two recoverability tests produce total impairment 25, leaving assets 35; adding both unadjusted shortfalls would double count 5.
Improved inflows reverse 15 without cash or early contract recognition; original allocated cost remains the reversal ceiling.
Group recognition uses remaining assets 35 and 15, yielding CSM 10 and 15. Premium receipt changes cash to 200 and liabilities to 110 with equity still 90.
Keeping acquisition assets and overstating margins together can still balance, so component and derecognition checks are necessary. No new defect observed.
